summary: Centralizes published-package groups, dependency propagation, and chart version bindings in one validated release manifest.
userImpact: Package and chart version mismatches are rejected before hosted release work starts.
Developers receive one deterministic version plan instead of discovering follow-up package bumps across repeated CI runs.
security: Release publication remains protected and continues to promote only exact qualified artifacts.
documentation: Documents the package-group manifest, generated version-plan workflow, dependency trains, and independent plugin release boundary.
knownLimitations: The planner validates and explains package changes but does not choose semantic impact for an author.
rollback: Revert the version-authority manifest and planner; existing immutable release receipts and published artifacts remain unchanged.
validation: Version-authority fixtures cover direct package changes, transitive packed-workspace consumers, semantic bumps, continuous release-range histories, chart bindings, and unrelated changes.
CI contract tests verify that the package-discipline lane invokes the deterministic planner.
